text.brief: In April 1965 Le Duan traveled to Beijing to ask the Party for support troops, and Liu Shaoqi agreed.
text.record: The Party sent engineering, railway and anti-aircraft units to North Vietnam from June 1965 and withdrew them by 1969 ([FRUS 1964-68, Vol. XXX, Document 115](https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1964-68v30/d115)). Chinese sources put the total who served at about 320,000, with a peak near 170,000 in 1967. American intelligence tracked the deployments, and Washington kept them out of public view.
text.reading: Both governments preferred silence, the Party to avoid a wider war and Washington to avoid a demand to fight one. Attribution managed by both sides is still Asymmetry, and it let the Party fight the United States at low cost.
text.gapText: Architecture Principles. The defender kept a combatant's role secret, so its public never weighed the true adversary.
text.fix: Decide attribution policy on a published standard, so silence is a choice with owners rather than a habit.
